title: Local densities and summable spectral coefficients
statement: Let μ be the Möbius function, φ Euler's totient, ζ the Riemann zeta function, and c=ζ(2)^(−1). All products below are over primes. For every integer q≥1 and integer l, the density g(q,l) from problem.md equals q^(−1)Σ_{m≥1, gcd(m²,q)|l} μ(m)gcd(m²,q)/m². Equivalently, it is zero if some p² divides both q and l; otherwise it equals (c/q)∏_{p|q}(1−p^(−2))^(−1)∏_{p||q, p|l}(1−p^(−1)). In particular 0≤g(q,l)≤1/q. Define the multiplicative function G by G(1)=1, G(p)=G(p²)=−1/(p²−1), and G(p^a)=0 for a≥3. Put γ(r)=cG(r), λ(r)=φ(r)γ(r)², and c_r(n)=Σ_{1≤a≤r, gcd(a,r)=1} exp(2πian/r). Then qΣ_{l=1}^q g(q,l)²=Σ_{r|q}λ(r), Σ_{r≥1}λ(r)=c, and, for every integer n≥1, the absolutely convergent series Σ_{r≥1}γ(r)²c_r(n) equals 𝔖(n)=∏_p(1−2/p²)∏_{p²|n}(p²−1)/(p²−2). There is an absolute constant C such that, uniformly for real R≥2, Σ_{r>R}λ(r)≤CR^(−1/2)(log(2R))² and Σ_{r≤R}rλ(r)≤CR^(1/2)(log(2R))².
cites: R. C. Vaughan, A variance for k-free numbers in arithmetic progressions (2005), Lemmas 2.5, 2.14, 2.15 and 2.17, specialized to k=2; https://doi.org/10.1112/S0024611505015352.

J. Brüdern, A. Granville, A. Perelli, R. C. Vaughan and T. D. Wooley, On the exponential sum over k-free numbers (1998), Lemma 3.1, specialized to k=2; https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/en/publications/on-the-exponential-sum-over-k-free-numbers/.
risk: The Fourier coefficient includes ζ(2)^(−1); omitting it changes both the density cancellation and the final constant. Residue classes not coprime to q must remain included.
